correctness.rationale: The cycle sample space is exactly labeled cyclic Euler tours of the triple-vertex graph; a contraction of two distinct edges is a bijection even if the replacement is a tagged loop. The degree-factor quotient is 1/(q-1), and the balanced contracted graph has all degrees positive even at q=2, so a zero tree cofactor correctly signifies no tour. The row Laplacian update is (e_s-e_v)(e_v-e_t)^T, including coincident vertices. Since P^3=J, the zero-sum inverse is (I+P+P^2-3J)/q; restricting to a root cofactor only adds a constant to the solution. I checked the three suffix/prefix bilinear forms in equations (2)–(5), including the coincident s=t when a=c, and their sum over the four multiplicities gives q^2-2-2/q. The constant word repeats its four-letter factor and is impossible. An independent binary enumeration via local successor permutations gave eight cycles with zero and eight with two palindromes, with each of 00100, 01010, 10101, 11011 present in four cycles and all others absent.
residual_risks: Binary enumeration only checks q=2; the reconstruction of the determinant argument is what supports general q. No formal proof-assistant verification was performed.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For a nonconstant abcba there is one length-two path using its distinct four-letter edges; all corresponding edge multiplicities in the theorem are one and the interior-vertex multiplicity adjustment is one. In unnormalized row-Laplacian notation the prior count formula is the cofactor ratio divided by q-1. Appendix B's inverse determinant reduces to 1+(e_v-e_t)^T L#(e_s-e_v) since the two-edge update is rank one. The ordinary inverse on the zero-sum subspace is the three-term geometric sum divided by q since P^3=J. Substitution then tests only zero, one and two shifts, giving exactly the three overlaps of the assigned proof. There is no additional count or structural lemma needed, and summing the exact indicator probabilities is immediate.

The count of a specified five-letter word is a zero-or-one indicator in this ensemble.
